plotSections.title: Raven's Razor
bullets: A feather-draped, anemic-looking dwarf tells Sylan the spirits were not attached to him: Sylan had already sent them on, and asks why Sylan is pulling them back. Sylan releases that pull and says he will not draw more back. They had claimed unfinished business, but he judges it is time they move on. The figure answers that they did, 'but she will say.'

The figure names Sylan Raven's razor and 'the pathway to the falls,' and says a razor of the Raven Queen has a duty to seek certain souls. The rest of that sentence is lost. Sylan thanks him and leaves.

Sylan reappears with rocks piled over his feet, the largest about pumpkin-sized, breastplate against his arm. He describes the ghostly passage as an experience he does not want to share, though he tells Gerk he could come some other time.

plotSections.title: Spirits of New Navel
bullets: Sylan believes walking through New Navel, including the last trip toward Carlkin's, inadvertently drew spirits to him. He remembers six souls, with descriptions but no names. His stated duty is to move souls on to the afterlife and to hunt those who refuse: people jealous of life, greedy, or trying to hold on. 'You cannot cheat her in the end.' He thinks that usually means undead, but also a spirit with no body. He is unsure what to do with good people who are not ready, and unsure whether taking them is proximity, a touch, or their time simply being up. He compares the pull to air into a flame.

He remembers no mayor, only a sheriff, and asks Gerk to have the sheriff put out word that any spirit willing to move on should find Sylan. He does not want to force anyone. Gerk agrees to look for the sheriff. Sylan plans to wait outside town so he does not collect more spirits, then go to Shades and Trades. He first thinks that proprietor was a living person, then decides the proprietor was a ghost he has been near before and has not taken.

plotSections.title: Carlkin's Lighthouse
bullets: Gerk goes into the city for the sheriff. The others fly to Carlkin's lighthouse. Glimmen and Araden land in the street and draw a crowd; Araden curls her wings and keeps her tail off the roofs, then sets Elrus down. Dana knocks as the point person.

Carlkin, the tortle, checks that Sylan and Gerk are not with them and that there will be no portals. He sees the copper dragon, confirms she is not Glimmen, and is startled and pleased that they brought Araden. He knows Benji from about the time the Sunder Chase began. Benji, a warforged the party already met in the Reach, pushes past Dana; Araden perks up, and Benji and Elrus embrace. Elrus has been training Walker and calls Walker over to meet Benji. Elrus and Araden had met the party at the gods' council, but Benji had not met Araden, Elrus, and the party together. Dana introduces herself.

plotSections.title: The Sunder Chase
bullets: Carlkin and Benji argue, warmly, over who gave whom the idea for the race, and over another copper dragon: one calls him a fool, the other says he is not, that he was an inspirational dragon, is still around, and is now a hoard dragon for that race. Entering on Araden would be treated as cheating and would disqualify someone from what they call a death race.

Carlkin says the party won the Sunder Chase and that he may have given them guidance. He credits Ord with a clever dispel against another ship, magic not seen in generations, and jokes that other crews rely on cannons, faster sails, or burning ships. Another approach he mentions is simply flying faster than the average ship.

chronologicalEvents: The feather-draped figure tells Sylan the spirits were not attached and that Sylan already sent them on, and asks why he is pulling them back.

Sylan releases the pull, asks why they followed him, and whether he must seek more souls. The figure calls him Raven's razor and the pathway to the falls, and starts to state his duty before the line is lost.
Sylan agrees not to pull more spirits back, says their unfinished business does not keep them here, thanks the figure, and leaves him.
Sylan returns with a pile of rocks on his feet and talks with Gerk, who has been collecting rocks. Sylan will not demonstrate the ghostly passage.

Sylan explains that he picks up spirits in New Navel, especially ones who refuse to move on, and asks Gerk to have the sheriff announce that willing spirits should come find him. Sylan will wait outside town and later visit Shades and Trades, whose proprietor he now thinks is a ghost he has not taken.
Sylan will try to remember descriptions of the six souls for the sheriff. Gerk leaves to find the sheriff.
The rest of the party flies to Carlkin's lighthouse. Glimmen and Araden land; Araden sets Elrus down, and Dana knocks.

Carlkin confirms Sylan and Gerk are absent, recognizes Araden as a copper dragon rather than Glimmen, and greets her. Benji comes out, Araden perks up, and Benji and Elrus reunite. Walker is introduced as Elrus's new recruit. Dana introduces herself; Benji is identified again as a warforged they met in the Reach during the Sunder Chase.
Carlkin and Benji revisit the start of the Sunder Chase, another copper dragon who is now a hoard dragon for the race, and Ord's dispel of a rival ship when the party won it.

Sylan.existing: Half-elf rogue and Gilbrick Gatekeeper, called Raven's razor.
notes: The spirits were not attached to him; he had already sent them on, and he stops pulling them back.
The emissary calls him the pathway to the falls and says it is his duty, as a razor of the Raven Queen, to seek certain souls. The description of whom is cut off.
Spirits told him they had things left unfinished. He answers that it is time for them to move on.
He returns from that place with rocks over his feet, the largest about pumpkin-sized.
He treats collecting and moving on the unwilling dead as his job, especially those jealous of life, greedy, or trying to cheat the Raven Queen. He is unsure about good spirits who are not ready.

He believes he gathers spirits by being near them, as when he last walked through New Navel toward Carlkin's. He pictures it as air drawn into a flame. He has not taken the Shades and Trades proprietor, whom he now thinks is a ghost.
He remembers six souls by description, not by name, and wants those descriptions given to the sheriff. He will wait outside New Navel rather than walk through it.
He invites Gerk to accompany him another time, but does not want Gerk there soon.
personality: Does not want to force spirits who are not ready, even though he believes overstaying is cheating the Raven Queen.
Keeps the ghostly passage private from the party.
quotesThemes: You cannot cheat her in the end.
They tried to tell me they had things left, but it is time for them to move on.
openQuestions: What should he do with spirits who are not the 'bad ones' but still do not want to move on?
Is a spirit taken by proximity, by touch, or only when their allotted time is up?

Raven emissary.existing: An unnamed raven who becomes a feather-draped person and calls Sylan Raven's razor.
notes: Appears here as an anemic-looking dwarf draped in feathers, in an empty place that is not the Abyss.
Tells Sylan the spirits were not attached and that Sylan already sent them on.
Calls Sylan Razor, Raven's razor, and the pathway to the falls.
Says a razor of the Raven Queen must seek out certain people; the rest of the instruction is not heard.
Checks that Sylan is not pulling the sent spirits back, and says of their unfinished business that 'she will say.'
quotesThemes: You are the pathway to the falls.
You are a razor of the Raven Queen. It is your duty to seek out those who...
openQuestions: Whom exactly did he tell Sylan to seek after the line cut off?

Raven Queen.existing: Elder god of death, also called Nira.
notes: Sylan's duty to seek souls is framed as hers: he is her razor, and 'you cannot cheat her in the end.'
The emissary says that although the spirits had unfinished things, 'she will say.'
Waits while Sylan is gone and passes the time gathering rocks. He declines to keep one, saying they make those every day.
Agrees to find New Navel's sheriff and ask for an announcement that spirits who want to move on should find Sylan.
Presses Sylan on how spirits reach him, how he would find the bad ones without entering town, and what happens to good spirits.

New Navel.existing: A familiar stop with Carlkin's lighthouse; its dead can linger in the city.
notes: Sylan says spirits are still walking the town and that his last pass through, toward Carlkin's, is how he picked some up.
The party remembers a sheriff there and no mayor. Sylan jokes that the party might as well be the mayor.
Shades and Trades sits in the middle of town, so Sylan will wait outside rather than cross the streets.
Glimmen and Araden landing near Carlkin's lighthouse draws excitement and a disturbance in the streets.

Shades and Trades.existing: Where Sylan found the staff later fused to Ord's lantern.
notes: Sylan means to go there after Gerk speaks to the sheriff, but only after waiting outside town.
He first says the proprietor was a real person, then decides the proprietor was a ghost. Sylan has been around him before and has not taken him.
openQuestions: Why has Sylan been near that ghost proprietor without taking him?

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like bookshop keeper at the lighthouse in New Navel.
notes: Opens the lighthouse only after something like a crate, a chain, and metal scraping. He is a tortle and immediately checks that Sylan and Gerk, and any portals, were not brought.
He recognizes Araden, is indignant he was not told she had been brought, and greets her. He can tell she is not Glimmen.
He and Benji go back to about when the Sunder Chase started. Between them, one gave the other the idea for it.
He says the party won the Sunder Chase, that he may have given them guidance, and he praises Ord's dispel of another ship as clever magic not seen in generations.
personality: Wary of Sylan, Gerk, and portals at his door.
Affectionate and argumentative with Benji about old races and dragons.

Araden.existing: A magically capable companion brought secretly to the Reach.
notes: A copper dragon, spoken of as she. She lands beside Glimmen near the lighthouse, tucks her wings, and keeps her tail from tearing roof shingles, then lets Elrus down.
She visibly perks up when Benji comes toward her. This is their first meeting.
Carlkin and Benji say racing the Sunder Chase with Araden would now be considered cheating and grounds for disqualification.
Rides Araden to Carlkin's lighthouse and dismounts at the door.
Greets Benji with an embrace, remarks that Benji looks old, and asks if he has been meditating longer. He introduces Walker as his new recruit.
He and Araden had already met the party at the council of the gods. He had not met Benji before this.

Benji.existing: Familiar with the Reach and previously met by the party.
notes: A warforged. He is inside Carlkin's lighthouse, pushes past Dana toward Araden, and embraces Elrus.
He and Carlkin have known each other since about the beginning of the Sunder Chase. He claims he gave Carlkin the idea, and he defends the other copper dragon as no fool.

He had not yet met Araden or had this introduction to Elrus and the party together. Dana introduces herself; the party already met him in the Reach, including at the Sunder Chase. Walker had not introduced them then.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter bonded to Glimmen.
notes: Elrus has been training him and calls him over as his new recruit to meet Benji.
He notes that Elrus and Araden already met the party at the council of the gods, and that those two had not met Benji.
Acts as the point person at Carlkin's door, knocks, and assures him that Sylan and Gerk are not with them and there will be no portals.
Explains that the copper dragon is Walker's mentor's dragon, not Glimmen, and that Walker has been training with an established dragon rider.
Introduces herself to Benji and recalls that he explained being a warforged and was with them for the Sunder Chase.

Ord.existing: Dragonborn paladin and Gatekeeper of Feldspar.
notes: Carlkin credits him with the clever move in the Sunder Chase: dispelling another ship, something not seen in generations. Carlkin says if anyone would have been disqualified for cleverness, it would be Ord.
Ord answers that someone else would have thought of it eventually. Carlkin says most crews think of cannons, faster sails, or burning ships instead.

Sunder Chase.existing: A summer seasonal event in the Reach.
notes: The party won it. Carlkin says he may have given them guidance, and Benji and Carlkin disagree over who first had the idea, dating their friendship to when it started.

Described in this conversation as a silly race and a death race. Usual tactics named are cannons, faster sails, and burning ships. Ord's contribution was dispelling another ship. Flying faster than a ship is mentioned as another approach.
Riding it with Araden would be considered cheating and would get a competitor disqualified. Another copper dragon is now a hoard dragon for the race.
A second copper dragon, not Araden, tied to Carlkin and Benji's history with the Sunder Chase.
One of them calls him a fool; the other says he is not, that he was an inspirational dragon, that he is still around, and that he is now a hoard dragon for the race.
openQuestions: What is his name? The transcript only preserves a garbled description.

newTerms.name: Pathway to the falls
notes: Title the feather-draped emissary gives Sylan, paired with Raven's razor, for his role moving souls on.

newTerms.name: Sunder Chase hoard dragon
notes: A copper dragon, not Araden, whom Benji defends and who now serves as a hoard dragon for the Sunder Chase. His name is not recovered.
